corrected_value.title: Extensive reading in English: habits and attitudes of a group of Italian university EFL students

decisions.quote:
The present study replicated the methods and data analysis of Crawford Camiciottoli’s
(2001) study on second language (L2) reading behavior of academic English-as-aforeign-language students. Using the original study’s questionnaire, we investigated 60
advanced non-academic English-as-a-second-language learners’ L2 reading frequency
and attitude.
decisions.reason: Both the shipped row and blind target 0 identify the same tested original study: Crawford Camiciottoli, B. (2001), 'Extensive reading in English: Habits and attitudes of a group of Italian university EFL students', Journal of Research in Reading, 24, 135-153 (References, lines 1062-1064). The conflicting_dois flag arose solely because the source PDF prints an Unicode en-dash in 'doi: 10.1111/1467–9817.00137' (line 1064) whereas the shipped record normalizes it to a standard ASCII hyphen ('10.1111/1467-9817.00137').

decisions.quote:
Our study revealed differentiated findings, while partially confirming Crawford
Camiciottoli’s results. In contrast to the original study, we found that the participants
with positive attitudes towards reading tend to read more and that experience in the
target-language culture and years of previous English study did not show statistically
significant results on the participants’ reading habits and attitudes. On the other hand and
in line with the original study, first language (L1) reading correlated with L2 reading
habits, and lack of time was the most selected reasons for poor reading habits.
decisions.reason: With the original identity resolved to Crawford Camiciottoli (2001) and the study type confirmed as a replication, both the Abstract (lines 21-27) and Conclusion (lines 1018-1025) state an explicit overall verdict of partial confirmation alongside contrasting findings ('partially confirming Crawford Camiciottoli’s results' while finding contrasting results for the attitude-frequency profile, target-language culture experience, and years of previous English study, and agreement on L1 reading correlation and lack of time). Under the codebook rules, this is 'mixed', matching both shipped and blind codings.

decisions.reason: The authors collected new questionnaire data from an independent sample of 60 advanced non-academic ESL learners in the United States to re-test the findings of Crawford Camiciottoli (2001), which surveyed 182 Italian university EFL students. Collecting new data in a different sample to re-test a published finding is a 'replication', matching both shipped and blind codings.
